summary.en: Venezuela is coping with severe earthquake damage to buildings, creating urgent humanitarian needs, while the United States has lifted sanctions on the National Assembly leader and deployed Space Force electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against the country. President Maduro and his wife face a delayed U.S. torture conspiracy trial scheduled for 2027, and the Trump administration is planning changes to Delcy Rodríguez's government and Venezuela's oil industry. A Dutch security report warns that Venezuela's instability could threaten Curaçao and the wider Caribbean Kingdom, and workers are demanding real wage recovery as the government weighs labor proposals. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Venezuela takler omfattende jordskade på bygninger, noe som skaper akutte humanitære behov, mens USA har opphevet sanksjoner mot lederen for nasjonalforsamlingen og har satt i drift elektromagnetiske og elektroniske krigssystemer fra Space Force mot landet. President Maduro og hans kone står overfor en utsatt amerikansk torturkonspirasjonsrettssak som er planlagt til 2027, og Trump-administrasjonen planlegger endringer i Delcy Rodríguez sin regjering og i Venezuelas oljeindustri. En nederlandsk sikkerhetsrapport advarer om at Venezuelas ustabilitet kan true Curaçao og det bredere Karibiske kongeriket, og arbeidere krever reell lønnsgjenoppretting mens regjeringen vurderer arbeidsforslag. To dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
